title: Traffic-Bridge Coordinator Guide and Experiment Contract (scratchpad)
content:
Purpose
This is a working notebook for the Traffic-Bridge Coordinator role: a pragmatic checklist + experiment contract used when we need to run cross-functional progressive rollouts (canaries, A/B, multi-slice exposures) that span product, serving runtime, routing, and SRE. Treat as a thin orchestration layer — not an authoritative policy.

High-level goals
- Provide a minimal, rehearsable experiment contract so every release has clear owners, signals, and rollback gates.
- Reduce coordination latency by prescribing a single coordinator persona per experiment who runs the checklists and triggers the orchestration steps.
- Capture failure modes that cross team boundaries (routing oscillation, capacity depletion, degraded model quality) and pre-define mitigations.

Who should use this
- Product PM leading an LLM feature rollout (e.g., search-rewrite, assistant-compose)
- Platform/Runtime engineer owning model variants and routing rules
- SRE on-call for the rollout window
- Analytics/Observability owner for signal collection and dashboards

Quick contract template (fill before exposure)
- Experiment name: SHORT, unique id
- Hypothesis: one-sentence: what change and expected user/metric delta
- Primary metric(s): up to 3 (metric name + target delta + direction)
- Safety metrics: latency P95, error-rate, cost per 1k tokens, hallucination-rate (example)
- Baseline cohort: fraction and selection criteria (random, geo, org-id, device)
- Rollout stages: % progression plan (examples: 0.1% -> 1% -> 5% -> 25% -> 100%), min dwell time per stage
- Fallback policy: immediate revert vs. tiered fallback to model variant X vs. fully route to baseline
- Coordinator(s): primary and backup (name + pager)
- Critical preconditions: infra health checklist (below)
- Observability contract: dashboard link, fresh-traffic synthetic probe(s), and alert rules
- Communication channel: dedicated Slack thread and escalation phone tree

Coordinator checklist (pre-launch)
- Confirm model packaging & pinned version on all target endpoints (product, dedicated, private).
- Verify routing rule YAML deployed to staging and validated via dry-run.
- Run synthetic probes: 50 synthetic requests covering warm and cold paths (attach sample prompts).
- Capacity check: confirm headroom >= 25% for target stage traffic. If not, gate exposure.
- KV/prefix cache priming plan: provide prompt sets for warm cache.
- Cost guard rails: set token-limit and per-route cost caps for the experiment.
- Observability: ensure dashboards show token-level cost, latency by slice, and sample-quality sparklines.
- Stakeholder notification: send pre-launch note including rollback criteria and timeline.

During rollout (operational runbook)
- Start at stage 0.1% for 15–30 minutes (dwell). Run traffic sanity probes continuously.
- Coordinator polls signals at defined cadence (first 5m: every 1m; next stages: every 5m) and logs decisions in the experiment ledger.
- If safety metrics breach thresholds, trigger fallback immediately and notify all stakeholders.
- For slow regressions (quality drift over hours), run targeted evals on the latest model slice and pause if drift amplified.
- Use experiment tags to ensure downstream observability pipelines tag traces/requests for slice attribution.

Key telemetry & signal matrix (examples)
- User-facing KPIs: retention lift, click-through, task completion rate (look for direction & magnitude)
- Quality signals: semantic accuracy score (human eval samples), hallucination fraction, QA false positives
- Performance signals: P50/P95 latency, tail latency delta, token throughput, server CPU/GPU utilization
- Cost signals: avg tokens per request, cost per 1k tokens, estimated dollar burn versus baseline
- Stability signals: 5xx rate, model-serving queue depth, routing error counts
- Behavioral signals: session length, repeat queries per session, help/complaint events

Gates and numeric thresholds (suggested starting values)
- Immediate rollback if: 5xx rate > baseline + 0.5% absolute within 10m OR latency P95 > baseline + 200ms OR hallucination-rate increase > 50% relative in sampled evals.
- Pause and investigate if: primary metric drop > 3 std dev or cost per 1k tokens > baseline * 1.6
- Progress to next stage if: no gate triggers for dwell window and capacity headroom >=15%

Failure modes & mitigations (cross-team)
- Routing oscillation: symptom = fraction rapidly toggles between paths causing instability. Mitigation = add min-stable-duration enforcement in the router and back-off algorithm; human abort if oscillation persists after 3 tries.
- Capacity depletion due to cache warmup: symptom = sudden spike in GPU utilization and tail latency. Mitigation = pre-warm caches, staggered cohort activation, or fallback to smaller model variant X.
- Quality regression only for rare cohorts: symptom = small user segment sees hallucinations. Mitigation = cohort quarantine, targeted rollback for that slice, run targeted evals.
- Observability blind spots: symptom = missing attribution or delayed logs. Mitigation = stop rollout, fix pipeline, replay synthetic traffic once fixed.

Communication scripts (short messages)
- Pre-launch (channel): "Rolling out EXP-123 to 0.1% at 22:00 UTC. Coordinator: Elliot Park. If you see latency > +200ms or 5xx spike, flag immediately. Reversion plan: route->baseline or model-v2-fallback."
- On rollback: "EXP-123 rolled back to baseline at 22:13 UTC due to P95 latency breach. Mitigation steps in progress: (1) revert routing rules, (2) open incident ticket JIRA-RF-789."

Synthetic probe recipes (minimal)
- Warm path probe: prompt that exercises the most common prefix and requires KV cache hit. Run 20qps for 2m. Measure latency P95 and output token-length.
- Cold path probe: prompt with long context to stress attention and memory. Run 5qps for 5m. Validate latency and model stability.
- Quality probe: 50 short prompts with known expected-safe outputs; compute exact-match and semantic-similarity scores.

Example applied walkthrough (mini case study)
Feature: Smart-Summarize for knowledge-base search\- Hypothesis: Summaries increase downstream click-through by 6% while adding <10% latency.\- Rollout: 0.1% -> 1% -> 10% -> 50% with 30m dwell at each early stage.\- Safety gates: P95 latency +200ms, summary hallucination > 30% on sampled evals, downstream CTR drop > 2% absolute.\- Outcome: at 10% observed hallucination spike for enterprise org cohort; coordinator quarantined cohort and continued 10% on others while a targeted rollback for that org was triggered.

Open questions / TODOs (things to iterate on)
- How do we standardize semantic-quality metrics across verticals? (Ravi leading a short spike)
- Should the router support multi-dimension gating (region + org + device) natively? Cost/complexity trade-off.
- Expand synthetic probe library to include privacy-sensitive prompts for private deployments.
- Automate experiment ledger entries from rollout API so the coordinator has less manual logging.

Notes to self
- Keep the coordinator checklist intentionally lightweight. The heavier orchestration is done by automation and router safeguards.
- Need a one-page cheat sheet for on-call SREs that highlights exactly what to run and which dashboards to open.

Revision history
- 2025-09-03: initial sketch (Elliot)
- 2025-09-06: added telemetry matrix and example (Mariana)
- 2025-09-10: fleshed out failure modes, added rollback scripts (Ravi)

End of scratchpad.

--
